q-287677.name: Question 1
q-287677.problem:
Consider the equation in the variable $x,$ given by

$$
2px=3x+5
$$

where $p$ is a constant. Given that this equation has no solution, what is the value of $p?$
q-287677.worked_solution:
Suppose we have an equation of the form

$$
ax=b
$$

where $a$ and $b$ are constants, and $b\ne 0.$ If $a=0,$ then the equation has no solution.

First, we rewrite the equation in the form $ax=b.$ 

We start by subtracting $3x$ from both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}2px & =3x+5 \\ 2px-3x & =3x+5-3x \\ 2px-3x & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we factor $x$ on the left-hand side. This gives

$$
(2p-3)x=5.
$$

Notice that this equation is now in the form $ax=b:$

$$
{{(2p-3)}_{⏟}}_{a}x={{5}_{⏟}}_{b}
$$

Therefore, the equation has no solution if

$$
2p-3=0.
$$

Solving this for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2p-3 & =0 \\ 2p-3+3 & =0+3 \\ 2p & =3 \\ \frac{2p}{2} & =\frac{3}{2} \\ p & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Suppose we have an equation of the form ax=b where a and b are constants, and b≠0. If a=0, then the equation has no solution.

First, we rewrite the equation in the form ax=b.

We start by subtracting 3x from both sides of the equation:

2px=3x+52px−3x=3x+5−3x2px−3x=5

Next, we factor x on the left-hand side. This gives

(2p−3)x=5.

Notice that this equation is now in the form ax=b:

(2p−3)⏟ax=5⏟b

q-288596.name: Question 2
q-288596.problem:
Consider the equation in the variable $y,$ given by

$$
(q+9)y=-6
$$

where $q$ is a constant. Given that this equation has no solution, what is the value of $q?$
q-288596.worked_solution:
Suppose we have an equation of the form

$$
ax=b
$$

where $a$ and $b$ are constants, and $b\ne 0.$ If $a=0,$ then the equation has no solution.

Notice that this equation is in the form $ay=b.$ In this case,

$$
a=q+9,\,b=-6.
$$

Therefore, the equation has no solution if

$$
q+9=0.
$$

Solving this for $q,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}q+9 & =0 \\ q & =-9.\end{aligned}
$$

q-288644.problem:

$$
(k-2)v-3=5
$$

where $k$ is a constant. Given that this equation has no solution, what is the value of $k?$

{{field-1}}

Suppose we have an equation of the form

$$
ax=b
$$

where $a$ and $b$ are constants, and $b\ne 0.$ If $a=0,$ then the equation has no solution.

First, let's write our equation in the form $av=b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(k-2)v-3 & =5 \\ (k-2)v-3+3 & =5+3 \\ {{(k-2)}_{⏟}}_{a}v & ={{8}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}

Therefore, the equation has no solution if

k-2=0.

\begin{aligned}k-2 & =0 \\ k & =2.\end{aligned}
